title: Digita sells consent-based data sharing as its whole premise, not as a feature
content:
Digita's offer is an integrated Solid product suite, and the research reads data ownership as its entire premise rather than as a feature attached to something else. The suite is described as delivering consent-based data sharing across government, health, energy and HR — four domains where the question of who holds the record and who authorised its release is the substance of the problem rather than a compliance wrapper around it.

Geographically it is Belgium's Solid-native supplier and it is active in both the Netherlands and Flanders, so it works both Benelux markets from one base. For a supplier search that treats the Dutch and Belgian tracks as separate, a lead already operating across both reduces the number of relationships needed to cover the region.

The commercial consequence is that no argument has to be made to Digita about why user-held data matters; that argument is its market position. What this record does not establish is anything about its engineering practice, size or delivery history — the assessment covers premise and geography only, and the lead sits at priority 2.
